utility.notes: SCE's own 'Incorporated Cities and Counties Served by SCE' fact sheet (updated 3/17/2025) explicitly lists 'Torrance' by name among the cities in its service area.

value.name: Southern California Edison (SCE)
value.notes: Clean Power Alliance's own homepage states it serves '38 communities across Los Angeles and Ventura counties' and names each one individually via its site's community directory; Torrance is not among the named communities. No other Los Angeles/Ventura County CCA serving Torrance was found, so Southern California Edison (SCE) is recorded as both the distribution and generation utility.

county.notes: Torrance is a well-documented Los Angeles County city; also listed under Los Angeles County in SCE's own service-area fact sheet.

permit_authority.value: City of Torrance Building and Safety Division
permit_authority.notes: Directly re-verified via browser this session (an earlier HTTP 403 to automated fetch was intermittent, not a persistent block).

permit_url.notes: Directly re-verified via browser this session, including the linked 'Torrance PV Automated Permitting Requirements' subpage (S7).

interconnection_url.notes: SCE's own Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page — a utility-wide fact already established for other SCE-territory records this session.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Southern California Edison (SCE), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by SCE across its entire distribution territory, which includes Torrance/Los Angeles County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC-administered SGIP program already confirmed for other SCE-territory records this session, reused as a utility-level fact.

required_documents.notes: Per the City's own 'Torrance PV Automated Permitting Requirements' page: 'Please make sure to have a roof layout, line diagram, and all data sheets ready before beginning the application form.' The City's separate 'Photovoltaic/Solar Permit Plan Requirements Checklist' PDF (which likely itemizes further requirements) triggers a file-download dialog rather than a viewable page and could not be read.

timeline_days.notes: The City's own 'Torrance PV Automated Permitting Requirements' page fully describes the automated-permitting eligibility criteria but does not state an explicit day count or 'instant'/'instantaneous' issuance language, so no timeline figure is recorded per the mission's strict explicit-evidence bar.

other_conditions: New PV system on an existing, permitted R-3 (residential) occupancy only; no existing PV or ESS already on the property
Ground-mounted systems, carports, and non-permanent structures are not allowed; flush-mount or non-hillside tilt-mount only
No trenching, structural modifications, or alterations to the structure allowed
Individual ESS max 20kWh, aggregate ESS max 80kWh, sited per California Fire Code setback/location rules
Projects not meeting the automated-permitting criteria may still submit for standard plan review via the online portal

permit_fees.notes: The City's page cites AB 1414 (2017), which caps what permitting agencies may charge for a small rooftop solar system (10 kW AC or less) at $500 statewide — this is a legal ceiling, not confirmation of Torrance's actual charged fee, so it is not recorded as permit_fees.
